title: Floor buffing with a rotary machine
audience: Trained cleaners and supervisors who operate a rotary floor buffer in any cleaning-group business.
learningOutcomes: Complete the electrical pre-use check and the pad check before buffing starts.
Select a buffing pad by colour, using the manufacturer's colour guide and the task.
Buff the edges first, then the middle, with the cable kept behind the operator.
Stop, unplug and check the pad halfway through the task.
Store the buffer and pads correctly after use.

instruction.heading: What buffing does and the risks it carries
instruction.body: Buffing uses a rotating machine and a pad to work the surface of a floor. It restores sheen and removes light build-up. The machine is heavy, spins quickly and draws a cable across the work area. Hands and feet are exposed to pads, base plates and any product used on the floor. The source states that only trained employees use electrical equipment, and the operator must be able to stop the machine at once. A trained operator treats the machine as a live hazard from the moment it is connected.

instruction.heading: Pad selection and condition
instruction.body: Pads are colour coded. The source notes that the darker the pad, the more abrasive it is. Choose the pad that the manufacturer's colour guide and the job specification call for, and do not choose by feel. Check the pad before you start, and turn or replace it when it is dirty or worn. Do not store the buffer with the pad and base plate still fitted.

instruction.heading: Electrical pre-use checks and the cable
instruction.body: The pre-use checks match “Safe use and care of electrical machines”: a valid test label, an intact plug, no bare wires or tape on the flex, and a safe socket. Keep the cable behind the machine at all times, so the pad never runs over it. Before you plug in, make sure the socket is switched off, and switch it off again before you unplug.

instruction.heading: Buffing sequence and pauses
instruction.body: Buff the outside edges of the room first, then the middle, starting from the point furthest from the exit and working back toward it. Halfway through, stop, unplug the machine and check the pad. Turn or replace the pad if it is dirty. After buffing, mop sweep the debris that has been pushed out from under the skirting boards. Before you leave, confirm the floor is clean, dry and not slippery, and that any wet area is signposted.

instruction.heading: Care after use
instruction.body: Safety check and damp wipe the buffer after each use. Wash the buffing pads and hang them to dry. Store the buffer upright in the position the manufacturer gives, with the pad off. Clean, well-maintained machines last longer and give a more consistent result, which the source ties to better service for the customer.

procedure: Run the electrical pre-use check and record it.
Choose the pad by colour for the task, check its condition, and fit it with the base plate in place.
Put on gloves and eye protection. Confirm the socket is off, then plug the machine in.
Route the cable behind you. Start at the edges, then buff the middle from the far point toward the exit.
Halfway through, unplug the machine, check the pad and turn or replace it.
Mop sweep the debris pushed out from under the skirting boards.
Unplug the machine, damp wipe it, and wash the pad and hang it to dry.
Store the buffer upright with the pad off, and record any defect.

workedExamples.situation: On a commercial floor the buffer's pad is worn and grey, and the job needs more cut than the pad seems to give.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not swap in a more abrasive pad on the spot without checking the manufacturer's guide and the job specification. Replace the worn pad with the one the guide gives for the task. If the job still needs more cut, tell the supervisor, so the method can be reviewed.

workedExamples.situation: A new operator wants to start buffing straight away, because the machine plugs in and runs.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop the operator. A machine that runs is not evidence that it is safe. Check the test label, the flex and the plug, and record the check. An untrained person does not use electrical equipment until trained, so the operator should not start.

equipmentAndPpe: Gloves for handling pads, base plates and any product.
Colour-coded pads and the manufacturer's colour guide.

commonErrors.error: Plugging in before the socket is switched off.
commonErrors.prevention: Socket off, plug in, switch on. Reverse the sequence at the end.

commonErrors.error: Continuing with a worn or dirty pad.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop halfway, unplug, check the pad, and turn or replace it.

commonErrors.error: Letting the cable run under the pad.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the cable behind you and out of the path of the pad.

commonErrors.error: Storing the buffer with the pad still fitted.
commonErrors.prevention: Remove the pad and store the machine upright.
Use the colour guide and the job specification.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Electrical equipment is tested and tagged as set out in “Safe use and care of electrical machines”.
Only trained people use electrical equipment.
Products used on the floor follow “Chemical competency: reading labels and safety data sheets”. Check the label and the SDS before use, and do not mix products.
The cable and any wet floor are trip and slip hazards for the whole area. Keep the cable behind the operator and signpost wet areas until they are dry.

qualityStandard: Pre-use electrical check completed and recorded.
Pad selected by colour for the task and checked; worn pads replaced.
Edges buffed first, then the middle, with the cable behind the operator throughout.
Pad checked halfway through; debris under the skirting removed.
Buffer stored upright with the pad off.
documentationEvidence: Electrical pre-use check record with test label date.
Operator training record for the machine.
Defect record, and a record of any pad replaced and why.
summary: Only trained operators use the buffer, and every use starts with the electrical check.
Select the pad by colour from the manufacturer's guide, and check it halfway through.
Edges first, then the middle, with the cable always behind you.
Store the buffer upright with the pad removed.

knowledgeChecks.question: How should a buffing pad be chosen?
options: By how it feels in the hand and how much it weighs on the machine
By colour, using the manufacturer's guide and the job specification
Whichever pad is nearest the machine and the one already fitted to it

knowledgeChecks.question: When should the buffer be stopped and unplugged during the task?
options: Only at the end of the job
Once the job is finished, so the pad stays clean for the next room
Halfway through, to check the pad and turn or replace it

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the correct storage for a buffer?
options: Upright, with the pad and base plate removed
On its side, with the pad fitted to keep the pad soft
Lying on the floor under the cable
